propositions: AST guards pinning a single hardcoded source file fail silently when the policed construct is moved to a sibling module by later refactoring, because the scan population no longer contains the target.

Four confirmed vacuous guards (findings 1-4) all lack anti-vacuity assertions and scan wrong locations after module splits: applier.py missing invariants imports now in apply_inbound.py, runner.py missing timeout code now in structured_run.py and agent_call.py, inbound_probe.py having zero rebar imports while mechanics moved to adapters/jira/probe.py, and usage_log.py containing zero string-parse calls while split logic moved to config.split_provider_qualifier.
Mutation testing confirms the repairs are effective: re-introducing the policed construct at its real current home causes the repaired guards to go RED, proving they are no longer vacuous.

The fix pattern requires both deriving scan populations from package transitive closure instead of hardcoding filenames AND adding anti-vacuity assertions with a landmark construct that must exist in the scanned population.
Finding 6 uses a relative pathlib.Path that breaks when pytest cwd is not the repo root; anchoring it to __file__ makes it robust to any working directory.
